title: Pontiac LeMans Engines by Year (1961–1993)
description: Every factory engine in the Pontiac Tempest and LeMans by year: the Trophy 4, aluminum 215, OHC six, 326 to 455 V8s, and the Daewoo-built LeMans.
intro: The Tempest and LeMans were Pontiac's compact and then mid-size cars from 1961 to 1981. The LeMans name returned for 1988–1993 on a small car built by Daewoo in Korea. The GTO began as a LeMans option and has its own page.
Pick a year to see every engine offered that model year, with its code, rated horsepower and the trims it came in. Each engine links to its full specs.
The first Tempest used a 195 cubic-inch four made from half of Pontiac's 389 V8, and offered Buick's aluminum 215 V8 and, for 1963, the 326.

The mid-size Tempest and LeMans used a Chevrolet-built six in 1964–1965, Pontiac's overhead-cam six from 1966 to 1969, and Pontiac V8s from the 326 to the 455. Ratings are gross through 1971 and SAE net from 1972.
The Colonnade and later LeMans used Pontiac V8s and, from 1977, engines from Buick, Chevrolet and Oldsmobile; the notes say which division built each one.
The front-drive LeMans was built by Daewoo with a 1.6 four and, in the GSE, a 2.0.
